articles.title: Ataque russo contra ônibus na Ucrânia deixa 30 mortos | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículo foi atingido em Kramatorsk, região no leste ucraniano que fica próxima à linha de frente de batalha local da guerra, segundo autoridades locais. Ucrânia fala em ataque deliberado a civis. Rússia não se pronunciou.
articles.summary: Veículo foi atingido em Kramatorsk, região no leste ucraniano que fica próxima à linha de frente de batalha local da guerra, segundo autoridades locais. Ucrânia fala em ataque deliberado a civis. Rússia não se pronunciou.
articles.body:
Carcaça de ônibus em chamas após ataque russo em Kramatorsk, no leste da Ucrânia, em 8 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/Vadym Filashkin

A Rússia bombardeou nesta quinta-feira (8) um ônibus com civis na Ucrânia em uma rua movimentada , segundo o governo ucraniano. O ataque, com uma bomba de precisão , deixou 33 mortos e 18 feridos , entre passageiros e pedestres, informaram autoridades locais.

O ataque ocorreu em Kramatorsk, cidade no leste da Ucrânia próxima a uma frente de batalha da guerra que a Rússia trava contra a Ucrânia há quatro anos e meio. Dois ônibus com civis circulavam na rua atingida pelo bombardeio, informou a polícia. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, disse que o veículo alvejado estava em um ponto de ônibus .

O veículo pegou fogo ( veja na imagem acima ). Imagens do local divulgadas pela polícia ucraniana mostraram corpos espalhados e a rua repleta de destroços.

👉 Segundo a Polícia Nacional da Ucrânia, a Rússia utilizou uma bomba aérea de precisão UMPB D-30SN no ataque . Esse tipo de bomba já havia sido usado em 2024 por Moscou para ofensivas contra alvos específicos, o que, na avaliação do governador de Donetsk, Vadym Filashkin, reforça a intenção de alvejar civis.

"Os russos atacam deliberadamente civis", disse Filashkin. "Para eles (os russos), um ônibus com passageiros é um alvo atraente justamente porque um único ataque pode matar o maior número possível de pessoas. Essas não são ‘consequências da guerra’. São pessoas mortas pelo Exército russo”.

O governo russo ainda não havia se pronunciado até a última atualização desta reportagem. Moscou costuma dizer que não alveja civis em seus ataques contra a Ucrânia.

Filashkin afirmou que suspendeu o transporte público em Kramatorsk e em Sloviansk por causa do ataque russo.

Carcaça de ônibus alvejado por ataque da Rússia em Kramatorsk, no leste da Ucrânia, em 8 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Governo de Donetsk

Destroços de ônibus em chamas e cadáveres em rua em Kramatorsk, no leste da Ucrânia, após ataque aéreo russo em 8 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Divulgação/Polícia Nacional da Ucrânia

O Exército russo intensificou, nos últimos dias, ataques com drones e bombas guiadas contra Kramatorsk e outras cidades da região, que ficam no chamado “cinturão de fortalezas” da Ucrânia.

A área é chamada assim por ser estratégica para as forças de defesa ucranianas no leste da Ucrânia — a região onde a Rússia concentra seus ataques desde o início da guerra. Antes mesmo do conflito, o governo de Vladimir Putin já falava em anexar o território.

Na quarta (7), um bombardeio atingiu um edifício residencial em Pryluky, o que Zelensky chamou de "presente de aniversário do Exército russo para Vladimir Putin" . Ao todo, 22 pessoas morreram no ataque , incluindo cinco crianças , e outras 54 ficaram feridas, segundo atualizou nesta quinta o líder ucraniano.

Nos últimos dias, Putin afirmou que puniria a Ucrânia por conta dos bombardeios realizados contra refinarias de petróleo russas e deu a entender que intensificaria os bombardeios quase diários contra o território ucraniano.

articles.title: El Niño: fenômeno pode ser o mais intenso desde 1950, diz ONU | G1
articles.standfirst: Fenômeno deve elevar as temperaturas em grande parte do planeta e alterar os padrões de chuva, aumentando o risco de secas e inundações em diversas regiões.
articles.summary: O fortalecimento do fenômeno El Niño deve elevar as temperaturas globais e intensificar o risco de secas e inundações extremas em diversas regiões do mundo.
articles.body:
Vista geral do leito do rio Mandrare, na região de Anosy, sul de Madagascar — Foto: RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA/AFP

O fenômeno El Niño continuará se intensificando antes de alcançar seu "ponto máximo" em dezembro, alertou a ONU nesta quinta-feira (8), ao advertir que poderá ser um dos mais fortes registrados desde pelo menos 1950.

Esse fenômeno meteorológico natural provocará um aumento das temperaturas em grande parte do planeta , segundo a agência de meteorologia e clima das Nações Unidas, e seu impacto agravará os efeitos da mudança climática causada pelo homem.

"O episódio de El Niño continuará se intensificando antes de alcançar seu ponto máximo, previsto para dezembro", afirmou a Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) em seu boletim mensal sobre o clima sazonal global.

"É provável que provoque temperaturas acima da média em grande parte do planeta e altere os padrões de precipitação, cenário em que aumentaria o risco de secas e inundações em diversas regiões", alertou.

O El Niño, como é conhecido o aquecimento da superfície do Pacífico equatorial central e oriental, é capaz de desencadear mudanças nos ventos, na pressão e nos padrões de precipitação em todo o planeta.

Em geral, ocorre a cada dois a sete anos e dura entre nove e 12 meses. As condições oscilam entre o El Niño e seu oposto, a La Niña, com períodos neutros entre um e outro.

El Niño "está se fortalecendo rapidamente"

"Prevê-se que as temperaturas da superfície do mar nas partes central e oriental do Pacífico tropical aumentem até atingir valores sem precedentes durante os meses de outubro, novembro e dezembro de 2026", afirmou a OMM.

"Isto se deve ao fortalecimento do episódio de El Niño, que vai determinar os padrões meteorológicos e afetar economias, ecossistemas e comunidades em todo o mundo", acrescentou.

Essa previsão baseia-se no consenso de 13 centros meteorológicos nacionais e internacionais de primeiro nível.

"El Niño se consolidou e está se fortalecendo rapidamente", ressaltou em comunicado a diretora da OMM, Celeste Saulo.

"Segundo as previsões da OMM, a probabilidade de que o evento persista até fevereiro de 2027 é praticamente de 100% e ele pode vir a ser um dos episódios mais intensos desde, pelo menos, 1950", apontou a especialista argentina.

Saulo esclareceu que El Niño não adiciona novo calor ao planeta, e sim libera aquele que está armazenado no oceano.

"As águas que alimentam o El Niño apresentam as temperaturas mais altas já registradas. Em outras palavras, há mais calor que pode ser liberado", afirmou.

O índice que mede as anomalias da temperatura da superfície do mar no Pacífico equatorial centro-oriental, a região que está no coração do El Niño, aumentou de 1,6 °C acima do normal em junho para +2,5 °C em agosto.

Para outubro, novembro e dezembro, prevê-se que a anomalia atinja aproximadamente 3,7 °C acima do normal.

Esse seria o valor mais alto desde o início das observações, ao superar o recorde anterior de 2,6 °C estabelecido em 2015-2016.

O último fenômeno El Niño contribuiu para que 2023 fosse o segundo ano mais quente já registrado e para que 2024 atingisse o máximo histórico, com cerca de 1,55 °C acima da média pré-industrial de 1850-1900.

Embora o El Niño geralmente alcance seu ponto de pico entre novembro e fevereiro, o aumento de temperaturas resultante costuma ocorrer mais tarde.

O episódio atual desse fenômeno já está afetando gravemente algumas regiões, entre elas a América Central, onde animais e plantações estão morrendo em razão da seca.

articles.title: Nobel de Literatura: relembre os vencedores dos dez últimos anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Anne Carson ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. O anúncio da premiação foi feito nesta quinta-feira (8).
articles.summary: Anne Carson ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. O anúncio da premiação foi feito nesta quinta-feira (8).
articles.body:
Anne Carson ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. — Foto: Reprodução

Anne Carson ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2026. O anúncio da premiação foi feito nesta quinta-feira (8). Segundo a Academia Sueca, a canadense Carson foi escolhida “por sua obra ousada e inventiva que, em diálogo lúdico com a tradição clássica, criou novas formas para a literatura contemporânea”.

Ao longo de toda a carreira, combinou a escrita de poesia com o trabalho de tradução e o ensino em diferentes universidades. A década de 1990 marcou a publicação de uma obra frequentemente apontada como a maior de Carson: "Autobiography of Red: A Novel in Verse (1998)". O livro demonstra sua notável capacidade de atualizar a tradição literária clássica. Com um olhar preciso para os modos de falar e as experiências contemporâneas, Carson parte de fragmentos de poemas do poeta grego Estesícoro, do século VI a.C., sobre o monstro vermelho alado Gerião.

Suas colaborações com artistas visuais, coreógrafos e diretores de ópera e teatro demonstram a liberdade com que ela se relaciona com as expectativas literárias e os sistemas de regras. É essa liberdade que está por trás da importância que sua obra, desde os anos 1990, adquiriu para o cenário internacional da arte e da literatura.

A escritora canadense Anne Carson na 75ª edição do National Book Awards no Cipriani Wall Street em 20 de novembro de 2024, na cidade de Nova York. — Foto: DIMITRIOS KAMBOURIS / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / AFP

Relembre os vencedores do Prêmio Nobel de Literatura na última década:

László Krasznahorkai, Nobel de Literatura em 2025 — Foto: Matt Dunham/AP

László Krasznahorkai ganhou o prêmio Nobel de literatura no ano passado. Krasznahorkai nasceu em 1954 na pequena cidade de Gyula, no sudeste da Hungria, perto da fronteira com a Romênia. Uma área rural remota semelhante é o cenário do primeiro romance de Krasznahorkai, "Sátántangó", publicado em 1985, que foi uma sensação literária na Hungria e a obra que marcou a ascensão do autor. Segundo o comitê, o escritor venceu “por sua obra convincente e visionária que, em meio ao terror apocalíptico, reafirma o poder da arte.”

Especializado em latim, ele se formou em direito na Universidade József Attila (JATE) (atual Universidade de Szeged) e na Universidade Eötvös Loránd (ELTE) (anteriormente Universidade de Budapeste).

Sua obra "Sátántangó" retrata um grupo de moradores desamparados em uma fazenda na zona rural da Hungria, pouco antes da queda do comunismo. O livro foi uma sensação literária entre os húngaros, transformado em um filme de Béla Tarr, em 1994. O autor recebeu diversos prêmios de prestígio, entre eles o Man Booker International Prize em 2015 pelo conjunto da obra.

Han Kang — Foto: AP Photo/Lee Jin-man, File

Han Kang, escritora sul-coreana, ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura em 2024. De acordo com a Academia, o prêmio foi concedido "por sua intensa prosa poética que confronta traumas históricos e expõe a fragilidade da vida humana". Seu livro mais famoso é "A vegetariana" , lançado no Brasil em 2018.

Han Kang nasceu em 1970 na cidade sul-coreana de Gwangju, e se mudou para Seul aos nove anos. Ela vem de uma formação literária, e seu pai é um renomado romancista. Junto à sua escrita, ela também se dedicou à arte e à música, o que se reflete em toda a sua produção literária.

Jon Fosse, escritor norueguês, ganhou Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2023 — Foto: Jornal Nacional/Reprodução

Jon Fosse, autor norueguês, ganhou o Nobel de Literatura de 2023 . Segundo a Academia, o prêmio foi concedido "por suas peças e prosa inovadoras que dão voz ao indizível".

Nascido em 1959, em Strandebarm, na costa oeste da Noruega, seu primeiro conto, "Han", foi publicado em um jornal estudantil em 1981. Dois anos mais tarde, Fosse fez sua estreia com o romance "Raudt, svart" ("Vermelho, preto", sem publicação no Brasil). Já chamado de "Samuel Beckett norueguês do século XXI", sua obra inclui ficção, poesia, ensaios, mais de 40 peças teatrais e títulos infantis.

Em setembro, a Companhia das Letras publicou "É a Ales" , que apresenta uma reflexão de amor e a perda a partir das memórias de Signe, uma mulher que espera seu marido, desaparecido depois de sair de barco em um fiorde.

Annie Ernaux — Foto: Julie Sebadelha/AFP

Annie Ernaux é considerada uma das autoras mais importantes da França , ao escrever romances sobre a vida cotidiana em seu país.

Professora universitária de Literatura, Annie escreveu quase 20 livros, nos quais aborda o peso da dominação das classes sociais e a paixão do amor, dois temas que marcaram sua trajetória. Sua obra, essencialmente autobiográfica, constitui uma radiografia da intimidade de uma mulher que evolui na esteira das grandes mudanças na sociedade francesa do pós-guerra.

Entre seus livros está "O Acontecimento" , de 2000, em que relata um aborto clandestino que fez nos anos 1960. A Academia afirmou que sua "narrativa clinicamente contida" sobre o aborto ilegal de uma narradora de 23 anos no livro continua sendo uma obra-prima entre seus trabalhos.

A estreia da autora foi em 1974, com o romance "Les Armoires Vides", que não foi lançado no Brasil. Ela só obteve reconhecimento internacional após a publicação de "Os Anos" , em 2008, com o qual ganhou o prêmio Renaudot. Sobre este livro, a Academia disse que "é seu projeto mais ambicioso, que lhe deu uma reputação internacional e uma série de seguidores e discípulos."

Abdulrazak Gurnah posa para foto em sua casa em Canterbury, Inglaterra — Foto: Frank Augstein/AP

Gurnah nasceu em 1948 e cresceu na ilha de Zanzibar, chegando na Inglaterra na década de 1960 como refugiado. O romancista começou a escrever aos 21 anos de idade e publicou dez livros e diversos contos ao longo da carreira. A temática de refugiados é a base de todo seu trabalho.

O romancista é conhecido sobretudo pelo livro "Paraíso" , de 1984, ambientado no leste da África durante a Primeira Guerra Mundial. A obra foi finalista na época do Booker Prize de ficção.

Louise Glück em imagem de novembro de 2014, quando recebeu o National Book Awards, em Nova York — Foto: Robin Marchant / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / AFP

Louise Glück, poeta americana, ganhou o Prêmio Nobel de Literatura 2020 . Considerada por muitos uma das poetas contemporâneas mais talentosas dos Estados Unidos, Glück é conhecida pela precisão técnica, sensibilidade e uma obra sobre solidão, relações familiares, divórcio e morte. Ela é autora de obras como "Receitas De Inverno Da Comunidade" e a coleção "Poemas (2006-2014)" .

Seus primeiros livros são centrados em casos de amor fracassados, encontros familiares desastrosos e desespero existencial. Nos trabalhos posteriores, ela continuou a tratar de temas como decepção, rejeição, perda e isolamento.

O vencedor do prêmio Nobel de Literatura de 2019, Peter Handke, em foto de novembro de 2018 durante uma premiação de teatro. — Foto: Georg Hochmut / APA / AFP

O romancista e ensaísta Peter Handke – que é coautor do roteiro do premiado filme "Asas do desejo" (1987) – foi escolhido ganhador do Nobel "por um trabalho influente que, com engenhosidade linguística, explorou a periferia e a especificidade da experiência humana", justificou a Academia Sueca.

O romance de estreia dele, Die Hornissen, ("As vespas", em tradução livre), foi publicado em 1966. A obra, junto com a peça '"Ofendendo o público", de 1969, são citadas como responsáveis por deixar a marca do escritor no cenário literário. Os trabalhos são reconhecidos pelas experimentações radicais.

Olga Tokarczuk posa com o Man Booker International no Victoria and Albert Museum em Londres — Foto: Associated Press

Sua estreia na ficção foi em 1993, com "Podróz ludzi Księgi" ("A jornada do povo do livro", em tradução livre).

Segundo o Nobel, a verdadeira inovação de Olga veio com seu terceiro romance, "Prawiek i inne czasy" ("Primitivo e outros tempos"), de 1996. O volume é "um excelente exemplo de nova literatura polonesa após 1989", avaliou o comitê do prêmio. No Brasil, obras dela como "Sobre ossos e mortos" foram publicadas.

Kazuo Ishiguro — Foto: Reprodução/Facebook

Considerado um dos mais importantes autores vivos da língua inglesa , ele é autor de oito livros (sete romances e um volume de contos). São de Ishiguro "Os vestígios do dia" (1989), que ganhou o Man Booker Prize, e "Não me abandone jamais" (2005), ambos adaptados ao cinema. Com obra versátil, já foi de registros de memória a ficção científica e fantasia.

Bob Dylan recebeu Nobel de Literatura — Foto: Vince Bucci/Invision/AP

A opção por um músico – e não por um escritor de ofício – soou incomum, mas o nome do Dylan vinha sendo cotado havia muitos anos. Também poeta e com diversos livros lançados, o artista é aclamado sobretudo pelo lirismo de suas letras.

articles.title: ‘Iran will never have a nuclear weapon’: Rubio draws red line for Tehran
articles.summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Wednesday that Iran will never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon under US president Donald Trump, as
articles.body: US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Wednesday that Iran will never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon under US president Donald Trump, as Washington pushes Tehran to make a substantial reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity as part of any deal to end the war.“Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period and end of story,” Rubio said at a joint press briefing with Greek foreign minister Giorgos Gerapetritis in Athens.“Anything they agree to that would be acceptable to the United States has to be something that ensures that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” he added.Rubio’s comments came a day after US Vice President JD Vance said Washington would not accept assurances from Tehran without concrete action on its nuclear programme. In an exclusive interview with Reuters, Vance said Iran must make a “meaningful” reduction in its enrichment capacity for the US to agree to an end to the seven-month war.“If you don't want a nuclear weapon, then why do you need 60% enriched fuel?” Vance said.“If you want to show commitment to not building a nuclear weapon, don't build highly enriched fuel,” he added.Vance said Washington remained open to a negotiated settlement but would not accept promises in place of action. The comments came as the US and Iran exchanged proposals aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial route for global energy shipments.The secretary of state also accused Iran of building up its conventional military capabilities to protect its nuclear programme from foreign attack. He said Tehran had amassed large stocks of ballistic missiles and drones capable of retaliating against countries that attempted to strike its nuclear facilities.Rubio said the Trump administration had significantly weakened those capabilities.“He destroyed their drone programme, their drone manufacturing capability,” Rubio said, referring to Trump.“He destroyed their missile capability. He severely eroded both of those capabilities in terms of current launchers. He destroyed their navy. He destroyed their air force.”Rubio said the weakening of Iran’s conventional military had reduced its ability to shield its nuclear installations from military action.“They will never have a nuclear weapon, period, not as long as president Trump is in office,” he said.US piles pressure on TehranRubio also painted a bleak picture of Iran’s economy, saying US sanctions were putting increasing pressure on Tehran.“Their economy is in total and complete freefall,” he said, blaming Iran’s leadership for spending the country’s resources on regional armed groups rather than its domestic economy.He specifically accused Tehran of funding Hezbollah, Hamas, the Houthis and militias in Iraq.Rubio said oil shipments through the strait had already recovered significantly.“There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: East Hampton wants to spend $36.3 million to buy 38.3 acres of a former New York sand mine once slated for a 50-lot commercial subdivision; 33.3 acres would instead become open space
articles.summary: East Hampton Town is moving toward a multimillion-dollar purchase that could dramatically change the future of a large former sand mine in Wainscott, New
articles.body: East Hampton Town is moving toward a multimillion-dollar purchase that could dramatically change the future of a large former sand mine in Wainscott, New York. The East Hampton Star first reported the proposed $36.3 million acquisition on October 1, while Long Island Life & Politics reported this week that the town sees the purchase as a way to preserve the property while retaining part of it for future municipal needs. The town is seeking to acquire 38.3 acres of the 70.5-acre property at 104 Wainscott Northwest Road. Under the proposal, about 33.3 acres would be designated for parks, recreation and open space, while roughly five acres would be reserved for municipal purposes. The town has not yet determined a specific use for that smaller portion. The property sits in the middle of Wainscott’s commercial area, north of Montauk Highway and near the headwaters of Georgica Pond. Its location has made the site a particularly significant piece of undeveloped land in a densely watched part of East Hampton.A major change from earlier development plansThe proposed acquisition would mark a sharp departure from plans that have occupied East Hampton’s planning boards for years. The property was the subject of the Wainscott Commercial Center proposal, which sought to divide roughly 70 acres of the former sand and gravel mine into 50 commercial-industrial lots. East Hampton’s own planning documents describe the site as a reclaimed 70.51-acre sand and gravel mine in a Commercial-Industrial zoning district.The development proposal became one of the most contentious projects to come before the town. A public hearing in 2023 lasted eight hours and was split into two sessions, according to The East Hampton Star. Earlier discussions also highlighted the unusual environmental characteristics of the property. The former mine has very shallow groundwater in places, with an earlier town discussion noting depths of as little as 2.3 feet. Officials and residents had considered how redevelopment could affect groundwater, drainage and the broader watershed around Georgica Pond.What the $36.3 million would coverThe proposed purchase would be the second-largest amount East Hampton Town has spent on a single parcel, according to The East Hampton Star. The town paid $56 million for a 30-acre property on Wainscott’s Main Street in late 2024. The financing would be split between two sources. About 86.95% of the purchase would come from Community Preservation Fund money for the open-space portion, while 13.05% would be financed through bonds for the five-acre municipal section.The town is also expected to amend its management and stewardship plan for Community Preservation Fund properties as part of the transaction. A public hearing on the proposed acquisition is scheduled for October 15 at 6 p.m., giving residents an opportunity to weigh in before the purchase moves forward.A property with environmental significanceThe site’s environmental importance has been part of the debate long before the current acquisition proposal. A 2022 environmental impact statement prepared for the commercial-center application described the property as a reclaimed former sand and gravel mine and examined the consequences of turning it into a large commercial subdivision.The Wainscott hamlet planning process had previously considered a range of alternatives for the property, including open space, recreation, shared parking, affordable housing, renewable energy and transportation improvements. The latest proposal would preserve most of the 38.3 acres rather than divide that portion into commercial lots. For now, the five-acre municipal section remains the biggest question mark. The town would retain flexibility over its eventual use while placing the overwhelming majority of the acquired land under open-space and recreation purposes.If approved, the deal would transform a property that spent years at the center of a commercial development battle into one that is largely intended to remain open, giving East Hampton control over one of Wainscott’s largest remaining tracts while leaving a smaller area available for future public needs.You use AI every day. articles.title: At 94, Indian Air Force is looking beyond fighter jets: What comes next
articles.summary: The Indian Air Force marked its 94th anniversary on Thursday, with the Air Chief using the occasion to reflect on the force's journey, the lessons of
articles.body: The Indian Air Force marked its 94th anniversary on Thursday, with the Air Chief using the occasion to reflect on the force's journey, the lessons of Operation Sindoor and the technologies that will shape its future. Describing the IAF as one of the most capable and professional air forces in the world, the Air Chief said its real strength lies not just in modern aircraft but in the airmen and airwomen who fly and maintain them.Tracing the force's origins to 1932, when it began with just four aircraft, the Air Chief said the IAF has since grown into a network-centric, multi-domain force. He paid tribute to veterans and those who made the supreme sacrifice, saying their contribution laid the foundation for the force of today.Operation Sindoor, conducted last year, featured prominently in the address. The Air Chief said the world watched the speed, precision and operational capability of the IAF during the conflict, with both its strike capability and air defence operations delivering effective results. Success in modern war, he said, comes not from weapons alone but from quick decision-making, accurate action and joint military coordination. The force's motto of being infallible, impervious and precise, he added, is not merely a tagline but a reflection of its preparedness and resolve.Training, according to the Air Chief, remains the bedrock of readiness. The principle of "we train as we fight" means aircrew and ground crew prepare to the standard of real missions, whether it is guarding national airspace, running disaster relief or conducting combat operations. This year, that preparation included Exercise Vayu Shakti, the Droneathon and the multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti, which he said were aimed at testing capability as well as speeding up the induction of new technology.On technology, the Air Chief said warfare is changing, with artificial intelligence, autonomy and digital innovation taking on bigger roles. AI is being used to analyse large volumes of data and help commanders decide better, while autonomous systems are being developed with human control retained. The aim, he said, is a technology-driven but human-centric force.Self-reliance, he added, remains the top priority. He pointed to the Tejas, the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft, the HTT-40 trainer, the Dhruv and Prachand helicopters, the Astra missile, the Akash air defence system and BrahMos as outcomes of that approach. The IAF is also working with ISRO and other domestic space agencies, and has a key role in the Gaganyaan mission, with space increasingly seen as an extension of the air domain.The Air Chief also highlighted the IAF's role in floods, forest fires and other disasters, at home and abroad, and the growing coordination between the Air Force, Army and Navy through joint planning and integrated operations.

articles.title: Who is Shiranthi Rajapaksa? Sri Lanka's former first lady arrested over alleged misuse of hospital funds
articles.summary: Sri Lanka’s former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa, the wife of former president Mahinda Rajapaksa, has been arrested over allegations of misusing LKR 10
articles.body: Sri Lanka’s former first lady Shiranthi Rajapaksa, the wife of former president Mahinda Rajapaksa, has been arrested over allegations of misusing LKR 10 million (approx 29.3 lakhs) linked to a charity she headed.The 73-year-old was arrested at her Colombo home on Wednesday by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC). She was later produced before a Colombo court, which ordered her to remain in custody until October 13 while investigations continue.What is the case against Shiranthi Rajapaksa?The investigation centres on Siriliya Saviya, a charitable organisation headed by Shiranthi Rajapaksa. Investigators allege that LKR 10 million obtained from the state-run National Savings Bank was meant to help provide a CT scanner to Colombo’s Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, but that the scanner was not supplied and the funds were instead misused.The case also involves former National Savings Bank chairman Pradeep Kariyawasam, who was arrested over allegations that the money was transferred to the Siriliya Saviya account without following proper procedures. He was later released on bail.There is a dispute over what happened to the money. Shiranthi Rajapaksa’s lawyers told court that the funds remain in the Siriliya Saviya bank account and have not been misappropriated. Her defence also said the organisation had been trying to raise about LKR 160 million for the CT scanner.Sri Lankan officials have also pointed to the fact that a scanner had already been donated to the hospital by China, raising questions over the purpose of the funds collected for the equipment.Rajapaksa has denied wrongdoing.Who is Shiranthi Rajapaksa?Shiranthi Rajapaksa was Sri Lanka’s first lady during her husband Mahinda Rajapaksa’s presidency from 2005 to 2015. She was closely associated with Siriliya Saviya, which undertook charitable and welfare activities during her years as first lady.Mahinda Rajapaksa dominated Sri Lankan politics for years, serving as president from 2005 to 2015 and gaining popularity after government forces defeated the LTTE in 2009, ending the 26-year civil war. His family subsequently became a powerful political dynasty, with his brothers, sons and other relatives holding key positions.His popularity waned amid allegations of corruption and abuse of power, and he lost the presidency in 2015. The family returned to power in 2019 when his brother Gotabaya became president, but his government was eventually overwhelmed by an economic crisis that triggered mass protests in 2022 and forced him to resign and flee the country.Why are the Rajapaksas facing corruption cases now?Sri Lanka’s current president Anura Kumara Dissanayake came to power in 2024 on an anti-corruption platform and pledged to pursue cases involving alleged wrongdoing under previous governments.His government has since revived several investigations involving members of the Rajapaksa family.Shiranthi’s arrest follows legal troubles involving her sons as well. Her eldest son, Namal Rajapaksa, a lawmaker and former minister, has been detained in a separate bribery case. Another son, Yoshitha Rajapaksa, was also arrested earlier this year on corruption-related allegations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2016, Cumbria began trialling waste-plastic roads; a year later, an A7 project reused 500,000 bottles or 800,000 bags; five years later, the trials were deemed successful
articles.summary: Kingstown Road and Scotland Road form one of the main routes into Carlisle, and by autumn 2017 they had a new skin.
articles.body: Kingstown Road and Scotland Road form one of the main routes into Carlisle, and by autumn 2017 they had a new skin. Some of the bitumen holding the asphalt together had been replaced with pellets made from waste plastic.Cumbria, an area in England, wanted to make roads the better way. Roads that are environmentally friendly. Regular roads use bitumen, which requires a lot of energy and materials and results in pollution. So, they did something extraordinary. They built a road using waste materials.The £200,000 project, completed by MacRebur in September, was one of several major road resurfacing projects in the county using recycled plastic.Regular roads had to goBitumen, the oil-derived binder in asphalt, carries a carbon cost. Companies such as MacRebur had a solution. They made waste plastic into small pellets that could be added to the material used to make roads. When the council came up with the idea of sustainable, eco-friendly roads, MacRebur suggested replacing a share of the bitumen with waste plastic that would otherwise end up in landfill or an incinerator. So, plastics equivalent to roughly 500,000 bottles, or 800,000 carrier bags, were used, depending on the yardstick.“We have been very pleased with the results. Using this waste plastic material provides a more sustainable solution for road resurfacing, and we will be using it in a number of locations across Cumbria’s road network,” County Councillor Keith Little said in a 2017 release.Stephen Hall, Cumbria’s assistant director for highways, transport and fleet, pointed out the environmental impact of regular roads and welcomed this new innovation. “Our industry has a significant environmental impact in terms of carbon footprint, use of oil-based products and the use of quarried material. I believe it is incumbent upon us to seek new and innovative ways to mitigate this impact, and using waste plastic in the road surface is something we have been very keen to support.”Showing the working to the Department for TransportCumbria did not keep the experiment to itself. Council officers shared their experience with Department for Transport officials, who were assessing new technology for highway upkeep.By 2021, the roads were part of the ADEPT SMART Places Live Labs Programme, a £22.9 million initiative funded by the DfT. Cumbria was allocated £1.6 million. It was one of just eight local authorities chosen, and the only one in the North of England.The programme’s aim was to encourage councils to try new highways methods on ordinary local roads, with the hope of changing how both the highways and waste industries work. Cumbria had a question: are additives derived from waste plastic sustainable and suitable for its surfacing programme? A smaller carbon footprint and a more resilient network were the goals.Shell joined MacRebur as a partner. Its Bitumen LTR binder uses chemically modified waste plastic that bonds with bitumen and lets asphalt be made and laid at lower temperatures, which cuts the energy used in production. It was the first in the world to trial MacRebur’s product and the first in Europe to trial Shell’s, according to the council.The Shell route arrived through surfacing partner Hanson Contracting, which approached the council about an additive from its bitumen supplier. In a final update published by ADEPT, Cumbria’s Matt Waning counted six live road trials and four quarry trials, with a five-year monitoring programme in place.The idea was about saving money and also reducing pollution. Diverting plastic from landfill and incineration saves on disposal, and swapping out bitumen can lower production costs, the council said. This technology could increase a road’s life cycle, which would mean resurfacing less often. This possibility matters. By October 2021, the council’s verdict was upbeat. It described five years of trials as successful, with products designed to make surfaces tougher and more environmentally friendly.Cumbria continues working with MacRebur and Shell, monitoring the plastic surfaces and drawing up a plan to extend the process to other roads in the county.You use AI every day. articles.title: Dr. Phil and Robin McGraw bought a Beverly Hills property for $29.8 million in 2010 and completed the mansion a year later; 16 years on, the 16,079-sq-ft estate is listed for $67.5 million
articles.summary: Dr.
articles.body: Dr. Phil McGraw and Robin McGraw are ready to part ways with their lavish Beverly Hills estate, more than a decade after transforming the property into a grand Mediterranean Revival-style mansion. The couple purchased the property for $29.8 million in 2010 and completed the residence a year later after a lengthy construction process. Now, 16 years after acquiring the land, the 16,079-square-foot estate has been listed for $67.5 million, according to Realtor.com. The asking price is more than double the couple’s original purchase cost and reflects the scale, privacy and extensive amenities of the sprawling compound. Set across 2.76 acres in the Beverly Hills Post Office area, the estate combines old-Hollywood glamour with the comforts of a modern luxury retreat. Read more details about their lavish house, as per Realtor.com, here:A major jump in valueThe property is being marketed by Billy Dolan of Carolwood Estates. If it sells close to the asking price, the transaction could give the McGraws a difference of approximately $37.7 million between their original purchase price and the current listing price. However, that figure does not include the money spent on construction, landscaping, later improvements, maintenance, taxes and selling expenses.According to Realtor.com, the couple bought the property in 2010 and completed the mansion in 2011. The residence was designed by architect Kevin Clark, although the construction process reportedly stretched across seven years. The result is not simply a large family home, but a complete private compound designed for entertaining, relaxation and accommodating guests.The estate includes eight bedrooms and more than 10 bathrooms across 16,079 square feet of living space. At the current asking price, the home is valued at approximately $4,198 per square foot, the report shared. Its size, location and collection of private amenities place it firmly among the most expensive celebrity properties currently available in the Los Angeles area.Mediterranean style meets modern luxury The mansion makes a dramatic statement with its Mediterranean-inspired architecture, grand proportions and ornate details. Inside, formal living and entertaining rooms have high ceilings, large windows and multiple fireplaces. French doors and expansive windows help to connect the interiors with the landscaped grounds, creating a sense of openness despite the home’s highly traditional design. The kitchen is designed for both daily use and large-scale entertaining. It features high-end Wolf and Miele appliances, as well as a butler’s pantry that provides extra storage and preparation space. An informal dining area offers a more relaxed setting than the formal rooms, while nearby doors open towards a patio surrounded by fountains.One of the home’s more distinctive features is its wine cellar. Accessed by a staircase decorated with herringbone-patterned brickwork, the cellar adds another layer of old-world character to the estate. The property also includes colourful wallpaper, chandeliers and richly decorated lounging spaces, reinforcing its elaborate, classic style.A private resort-like compoundThe estate’s design extends well beyond the main residence. The compound has dedicated staff facilities and a guesthouse, providing staff and visitors their own space but with privacy within the main house. This is an ideal design for a property of this size, allowing entertainment and household activities to take place independently of the owners. The primary suite functions as a private sanctuary rather than just a bedroom. It features a sitting area, separate bathrooms and large wardrobe areas. The extra room allows the suite to be a self-contained part of the mansion, with room for both leisure and personal activities.Outside, the grounds have been extensively landscaped to create a secluded setting. A large swimming pool serves as the centrepiece of the outdoor entertainment area, while the property’s elevated position offers views of the surrounding city skyline and nearby mountains. The grounds are designed to feel more like a private resort than a conventional backyard.Pool, tennis court and expansive groundsSports and recreation are also central to the estate’s appeal. The property includes a clay tennis court accompanied by an entertainment pavilion, creating a dedicated space for both games and social gatherings. A four-car garage and large motor court provide ample room for vehicles, guests and arrivals.Together, the pool, tennis court, pavilion, guesthouse, staff quarters and landscaped grounds give the property an unusually comprehensive character. For the next owner, the mansion offers the privacy of a gated retreat while remaining close to the lifestyle and prestige associated with Beverly Hills.The current listing also comes at a time when the McGraws continue to hold a substantial property portfolio. Realtor.com reported that the couple owns several other California residences, including a Calabasas mansion purchased in 2011 for $6.6 million and another Beverly Hills property bought for $10 million in 2020. That home is understood to be used mainly by their son Jordan McGraw and his wife, Morgan Stewart.The couple also owns a mansion in Dallas, which Dr. Phil purchased in 2020 after it had been listed for just under $12 million. Their Beverly Hills estate, however, remains the most ambitious property in the portfolio now being offered to the market.At $67.5 million, the residence is aimed at a buyer seeking more than square footage. It offers a complete luxury lifestyle, with grand architecture, private guest facilities, resort-style outdoor spaces and a location associated with celebrity Los Angeles. Whether the property achieves its full asking price will depend on the market and the buyer’s appetite for a highly personalised estate, but the listing already highlights the remarkable rise in value of the home since the McGraws purchased it in 2010.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Prince William's charitable foundation funded homes on Duchy land in Cornwall; in August, the first phase was handed to a charity, providing accommodation and support for 16 people facing homelessness
articles.summary: A new housing project in Cornwall is putting a different face on the fight against homelessness.
articles.body: A new housing project in Cornwall is putting a different face on the fight against homelessness. Rather than treating shelter as a temporary stopgap, the development in Nansledan, Newquay, combines carefully designed homes with practical support, creating a more secure route towards independent living for people who have experienced homelessness. Scroll down to read the details.A new beginning in NansledanAccording to the Nansledan website, on August 4, 2026, St Petrocs received the keys to the first phase of the development from the Duchy of Cornwall. Funded by The Duke of Cornwall’s Charitable Foundation and built on Duchy-owned land, the scheme will provide accommodation for 16 people across two four-bedroom homes and eight one-bedroom apartments.Built by CG Fry & Son, the development was designed around more than simply providing a roof. On-site counselling space will allow St Petrocs to offer residents support alongside their accommodation, helping them establish greater stability as they work towards securing permanent housing, adds the report. The handover marks the completion of the construction phase and the beginning of the homes’ next chapter, with residents set to move into fully equipped properties, the report adds.Housing with support at its coreThe project forms part of Homewards, The Royal Foundation’s five-year programme established by The Duke of Cornwall with the ambition of demonstrating that homelessness can be prevented and made rare, brief and unrepeated. The programme brought the Duchy together with homelessness prevention specialists and people with lived experience, helping shape the design and approach to the development. The result is a model that places housing, wellbeing and community connection on the same footing.For St Petrocs, which supports people experiencing homelessness in Cornwall, the homes offer a chance to provide continuity rather than short-term intervention. Residents will have access to personalised support while becoming part of the wider Nansledan community.Designed for a lower-carbon futureAs per the report, sustainability is another defining feature of the project. The all-electric homes have been constructed with a focus on reducing both embodied carbon and the emissions associated with everyday use. Ultra-low-carbon cement and blockwork, super-insulated hemp-filled wall panels and solar panels form part of the environmental strategy. The approach is intended not only to reduce the development’s impact but also to keep future running costs lower for St Petrocs.The homes have also been furnished through the Homewards Furniture Project, with support from retailers and partners including Howdens, IKEA, DFS, B&Q, Bosch Home Appliances and Gordon Brown’s The Multibank charity. Sofas, tables, chairs, white goods and fitted kitchens mean residents can move into spaces that are ready to live in from day one.A wider community taking shapeNansledan itself reflects the Duchy’s broader approach to sustainable development. The urban extension to Newquay combines homes with shops, businesses, community facilities, green spaces and walkable neighbourhoods. The supported housing scheme adds another dimension to that vision: ensuring that those at risk of being left on the margins can also find a place within a growing community.As the first residents prepare to move in, the project represents the Duchy of Cornwall’s first housing development specifically designed to address homelessness. Its significance lies not just in the number of homes created, but in the idea behind them: that secure accommodation, meaningful support and a sense of belonging can work together to help people rebuild their lives.Images Courtesy: BBC and Royal FoundationYou use AI every day. articles.title: Prince William launches Amazon partnership to protect Indigenous defenders; partner reaches 110 million hectares, with DiCaprio's video support
articles.summary: In November 2025, Prince William used the stage of the fourth annual United for Wildlife Global Summit in Rio de Janeiro to unveil a new alliance for the
articles.body: In November 2025, Prince William used the stage of the fourth annual United for Wildlife Global Summit in Rio de Janeiro to unveil a new alliance for the people who defend the Brazilian Amazon. The partnership aims to protect Indigenous leaders and nature defenders working across territory covering 110 million hectares. Actor and environmentalist Leonardo DiCaprio added his voice to the occasion through a surprise video message. The initiative arrived days before the United Nations climate conference in Belém, at a time when destruction of the rainforest and violence against its guardians were rising. Here is what it promises.What Prince William announced at the 2025 United for Wildlife Global Summit in BrazilUnited for Wildlife reported that on Tuesday, 4 November 2025, the Prince of Wales unveiled an ambitious initiative to partner with Indigenous Peoples and nature protectors across the Brazilian Amazon and to strengthen their protection. The strategic partnership brings together The Royal Foundation's United for Wildlife programme, the Coordination of Indigenous Organisations of the Brazilian Amazon, the Podáali Fund, Rainforest Foundation Norway (RFN) and Rewild.In his keynote address, Prince William told the summit audience: "We cannot manage our forests while their protectors live in fear." He added that the initiative means working alongside those who know the land best, strengthening Indigenous-led systems and delivering legal aid and emergency support.Leonardo DiCaprio appeared by surprise video message and urged world leaders to take urgent actionThe summit had a surprise guest. People reported that DiCaprio, then 50, joined the Prince of Wales, then 43, by video message on 4 November. He told leaders at the meeting that the time to act had come. People also reported that Prince William unveiled a plan to help those striving to protect Indigenous people who are losing their livelihoods to deforestation.The video was also published on DiCaprio's Instagram page, and the Oscar winner said, "Nature is our most powerful solution." DiCaprio was not named as a partner in the initiative. His message gave added profile to its cause.Why the Amazon needs protecting: Illegal logging, gold mining, land-grabbing and threats to defendersAccording to United for Wildlife, the Amazon faces a double crisis of accelerating environmental destruction and escalating violence against those who protect it. In 2024, more than 1.7 million hectares of rainforest were cleared, much of it driven by illegal logging, gold mining and land-grabbing.Satellite analysis published in June 2025 by the Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program, using University of Maryland data, shows how far the damage reached. It found that deforestation across all nine Amazon countries in 2024 was the fifth highest since 2002, a 34 per cent jump from 2023, with Brazil responsible for 54.7 per cent of the total and Bolivia for 27.3 per cent. Fire made 2024 even worse, blazes damaged a record 2.8 million hectares of primary forest, and Brazil and Bolivia accounted for 95 per cent of that damage. Deforestation and fire together affected 4.5 million hectares, the highest combined total ever recorded. The programme noted that agriculture and gold mining drove most deforestation hotspots without major fires.Indigenous communities, whose lands host approximately 27 per cent of the Brazilian Amazon, bear the damage to their livelihoods, ancestral lands and sacred sites. Their stewardship works: United for Wildlife noted that deforestation in Indigenous lands is up to 83 per cent lower than in unprotected areas.The people doing that work face growing danger. In 2023 and 2024, 393 cases of violence against environmental defenders were recorded in Brazil. Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities were disproportionately affected, accounting for around a third of those killed or who disappeared in 2024.How the partnership will work across nine states and shared threat dataAccording to United for Wildlife, the partnership seeks to break down barriers to the safety of Indigenous leaders across nine states of the Brazilian Amazon. It will prioritise wider access to legal support and an emergency response fund to help people at risk reach safety, whether through emergency evacuation, secure communications, safe houses or humanitarian aid.The partnership will also raise global awareness of Indigenous Peoples' rights and their vital role in protecting the Amazon, and will improve the monitoring of threats through a shared data platform.What 110 million hectares means, the scale of Indigenous territory reached by the Amazon partnershipThe scale comes from the Indigenous partner at its centre. United for Wildlife said the Coordination of Indigenous Organisations of the Brazilian Amazon reaches 750,000 Indigenous people across approximately 110 million hectares of Amazon territory.Its Executive Coordinator, Toya Manchineri, told the summit that the safety of those who defend the forests with their own lives must be central to global discussions. For Indigenous peoples, he said, the territory is sacred, a place where the spiritual and the material come together. He described protecting it as a mission inherited from ancestors and invited the world to join the struggle.Doctor Tom Clements, Executive Director of United for Wildlife, said that protecting the land and resources of Indigenous Peoples and local communities is one of the most effective ways to protect nature and fight climate change. He stressed that the initiative is built and led by Indigenous-governed delivery mechanisms, offering a model for how the global community can support nature protectors everywhere.You use AI every day. articles.title: 3 years, 50,000 rifles later: Why US Army is moving on from the M7
articles.summary: The US Army is moving on from the M7 rifle barely three years after beginning to field it, with soldier feedback over the weapon's weight, length and
articles.body: The US Army is moving on from the M7 rifle barely three years after beginning to field it, with soldier feedback over the weapon's weight, length and handling driving the development of a new M8 carbine. The Army is set to begin fielding the M8 in December, marking a rapid redesign of its Next Generation Squad Weapon system.According to Defense News, citing Sig Sauer executives, the M8 will initially be fielded with units at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. The weapon, earlier designated the XM8, is a shorter and lighter variant of the M7 developed after soldier feedback and Army testing.The M7's weight has been one of the major concerns. The rifle weighs more than 8 pounds (3.6 kg) unloaded and nearly 10 pounds (4.5 kg) with its suppressor, significantly heavier than the Army's M4A1. Soldiers also raised concerns about the weapon's length and handling while carrying it alongside their other combat equipment.The M8 is designed to address those problems without abandoning the Army's new 6.8mm weapon concept. The Army says the M8 is more than a pound (0.45 kg) lighter and has a barrel 3.5 inches (8.9 cm) shorter than the M7, while retaining the 6.8×51mm ammunition and compatibility with the M157 fire-control system.Defense News reported that the Army's fiscal 2027 budget request seeks 14,944 M8 carbines but no additional M7 rifles, even though roughly 50,000 M7s have already been delivered.Why soldiers wanted a lighter rifleThe M7 was introduced as a major upgrade over the M4, but its increased size and weight created a practical problem for infantrymen. The rifle's heavier configuration adds to the overall load soldiers already carry in body armour, ammunition, optics, communications equipment and other battlefield gear, making mobility a key concern.According to Defense News, the Army's experience with the M7 led to feedback on its weight and length, while soldiers also raised concerns about component wear linked to the weapon's high-pressure ammunition. The M8 was subsequently developed with a shorter barrel and lighter configuration to address those concerns.Sig Sauer executive Dave Buehler said the M8 allowed the company to incorporate feedback that could not easily be addressed in the original M7 design because of the Army's initial programme requirements. He described the M8 as a significantly improved version of the weapon.The M8 also has a fixed stock instead of the M7's folding stock, a redesigned handguard and changes intended to improve the weapon's balance and ergonomics, according to Sig Sauer and Army documentation.Meet the M8 rifleThe M8, formerly designated the XM8, is a lightweight, short-barrel variant of the M7 developed by Sig Sauer for the US Army’s Next Generation Squad Weapon programme.The Army describes it as a modular, piston-driven, select-fire, magazine-fed 6.8mm rifle designed to give close-combat troops greater mobility while retaining the lethality of the 6.8×51mm ammunition.The M8 weighs 7.3 pounds (3.3 kg) empty and 8.8 pounds (4 kg) with its suppressor and heat shield, according to the US Army. It is more than 1 pound (0.45 kg) lighter than the M7 and approximately 3.5 inches (8.9 cm) shorter.The M8 uses a free-floating M-LOK handguard, allowing soldiers to mount accessories while keeping the barrel free from contact with the handguard.The M8 retains universal compatibility with the M157 Small Arms Fire Control system. The M157 combines a variable-magnification optic with a laser rangefinder, ballistic calculator, atmospheric sensors, compass, visible and infrared aiming lasers and a digital display overlay.The M157 weighs 2.67 pounds (1.21 kg) and has 1–8x magnification, according to the Army. It is designed to provide soldiers with a calculated ballistic solution and corrected point of aim, including for engagements beyond 600 metres.

articles.title: Marriage fraud, duplicate identity: 4 Pakistani men to lose US citizenship in largest denaturalization move by the Trump administration
articles.summary: Among the 40 men who will lose their US citizenship in the Donald Trump administration's largest denaturalization move, four are from Pakistan.
articles.body: Among the 40 men who will lose their US citizenship in the Donald Trump administration's largest denaturalization move, four are from Pakistan. Attorney General Todd Blanche called this the largest denaturalization effort in modern history. All of them lied to obtain US citizenship, used several identities to conceal their criminal past.Ahmad Bahar Khattak (69): Ahmad Bahar Khattak, also known as Bahar Ahmad and Said Umar Khan, allegedly became a US citizen in Virginia illegally in spite of pre-existing removal proceedings. He changed his identity and prior deportation history, the Justice Department said."Ahmad Bahar Khattak illegally procured his naturalization and willfully concealed material facts by engaging in a multi-decade fraudulent scheme utilizing dual identities to evade deportation and secure immigration benefits. Specifically, after an Immigration Judge ordered Ahmad Bahar Khattak excluded in absentia in 1994 under the alias of Said Umar Khan, he concurrently applied for immigration benefits and ultimately naturalized on March 20, 2008, under the identity of Bahar Ahmad without disclosing his prior exclusion order," the court document said.Following his naturalization, he continued his deceptive conduct by leveraging his unlawfully acquired status to obtain US passports and sponsor family members for immigration benefits.Ahmed Khan (73): Ahmed Khan is accused of marriage fraud in Ohio. After arriving in the United States from Pakistan in 1999, Khan secured a bogus death certificate for his still-living Pakistani wife and then married a US citizen. Relying on that bigamous marriage, Khan obtained permanent residence in 2002 by falsely representing both the death of his Pakistani wife and that he did not plan to practice polygamy in the United States. According to a Justice Department document, his misrepresentations at the start of his immigration journey made him inadmissible and ultimately ineligible for US citizenship. Khan nevertheless unlawfully naturalized as a US citizen in 2008 by failing to disclose his ongoing marriage to his Pakistani wife; providing false testimony during his naturalization interview; committing unlawful acts, including immigration fraud, that adversely reflected on his moral character; and willfully misrepresenting material facts about his marriage history and other matters throughout his naturalization proceedings.Syed Mashood Ul Haque (66): Ul Haque entered the United States on a tourist visa in 1993 under his current identity, then overstayed this visa. In 1994, Ul Haque used the identity “Mashud Ahmad” to apply for asylum. When the government denied his asylum application, he failed to appear for his immigration hearing and evaded lawful deportation. After remaining illegally in the United States for decades, Ul Haque used his current identity to take advantage of a family-based immigration petition and become a permanent resident in 2005. Ul Haque later naturalized as a US citizen in Florida.Syed Furqan Ali (74): In 1993, Ali sought naturalization in Texas based on his marriage to a US citizen while still married to his first wife, a citizen of Pakistan. Ali had fabricated his divorce and former wife’s death to gain admission to the United States. The complaint against Ali alleged five counts that include his unlawful adjustment as a permanent resident and false testimony at his naturalization interview that he was divorced and legally married to his second wife at the time of his admission into the United States.You use AI every day. articles.summary: The FBI arrested an 18-year-old Minnesota man on Tuesday after nearly two years of tracking him over an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting at the
articles.body: The FBI arrested an 18-year-old Minnesota man on Tuesday after nearly two years of tracking him over an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting at the Mall of America near Minneapolis.Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud was taken into custody after an undercover FBI agent allegedly sold him an AK-47, ammunition and magazines for $600, according to the criminal complaint.Investigators allege Mohamud told the undercover informant that he planned to use the weapon to kill between 30 and 60 people at an event at the mall in late October.A nearly two-year investigationAccording to a court document posted by the US department of Justice, the FBI had been investigating Mohamud since about December 2024. Over roughly 21 months, the department says, Mohamud and a confidential human source exchanged hundreds of messages across social media and encrypted messaging platforms.According to the document, those messages were ones "wherein MOHAMUD expressed his desire to travel to Somalia to join a Foreign Terrorist Organisation (FTO) and fight on its behalf and/or to commit a mass-casualty attack on behalf of an FTO in Minnesota by acquiring and using a firearm and ammunition".The contact began in or about December 2024, the department said, when the source, referred to as CHS1, started exchanging messages with Mohamud. The two communicated directly on the encrypted appsTelegram and Signal, and on the social media platforms Discord and TikTok. On Signal, the document notes, Mohamud used the account "Mister Miser".Mohamud allegedly told the source across various platforms that he wanted to travel abroad to fight for al-Shabaab, a designated foreign terrorist organisation. He said that, if he could not go, he would carry out a mass shooting instead. He later said he wanted to join ISIS.He also reportedly was in favour of the man who drove a truck into a crowd in New Orleans on January 1, 2025, killing 14 people.In July, Mohamud allegedly said he intended to kill 30 to 60 people at the Mall of America as the owners were Jewish and said he wanted to kill non-Muslims.Mohamud reportedly told the informant he had planned the attack for October 24 because a "Hmong Arts Celebration" was being held at the mall that day.The Mall of America is the largest shopping centre in the United States, with over 500 stores.You use AI every day. articles.title: UN-doing the United Nations: Can its next chief fix a system under severe strain?
articles.summary: 'If you ever feel useless, remember; the United Nations exists,' goes a viral meme, reflecting the growing frustration over the organisation's inability
articles.body: 'If you ever feel useless, remember; the United Nations exists,' goes a viral meme, reflecting the growing frustration over the organisation's inability to resolve major global conflicts.As usual, the ongoing 81st UN General Assembly has seen a succession of mostly monologues, with many of the world's major leaders already taking their turn at the podium, against the familiar backdrop of green serpentinite, in New York.In the competitive and chaotic world order, ranging from the multilateral to bipolar, sides have been chosen and the usual calls for peace, cooperation and a "rules-based international order" have been made. Including the walkouts.Nonetheless, the demanding question is how much the UN, in its current state, can accomplish? After a month into the 81st session, which of today's wars or conflicts is actually "listening" to the UN?Missiles and drones have devastated communities in Iran, Israel, Russia and Ukraine, while civil conflicts burn on in Myanmar and Sudan. The Security Council has repeatedly struggled to act, with China, Russia or the United States, three of its five veto-wielding powers, blocking action on major conflicts.These divisions have exposed the limits of the UN and its Security Council, which has struggled to act when the interests of its five permanent members collide.The Trump administration also halted much of its funding for UN activities last year, forcing cuts to peacekeeping and relief work. The bigger concern is whether the UN can still translate its words and resolutions into meaningful action on the ground.The paradox of promisesCreated in 1945 after two devastating world wars, the United Nations was designed to prevent another global catastrophe, provide a forum where countries could resolve disputes and give weaker countries a voice in an international system dominated by powerful nations. Eight decades later, that system is under severe strain.The global platform once strongly voiced in the support of decolonisation, delivered humanitarian assistance, facilitated peace operations and provided a platform where even the smallest countries can speak.In 1962, UN third secretary general U Thant acted as a key neutral mediator during the Cuban Missile Crisis, helping the US and Soviet Union pull back from nuclear war.However, against the ambitions of sixth secretary general Boutros Boutros-Ghali, who after the end of the Cold War, had thought to achieving the "rule-based order", the world witnessed Rwandan genocide in 1994 and the Srebrenica massacre in Bosnia in 1995, bone-chilling atrocities that blue helmet peacekeepers failed to prevent.Later, seventh secretary general Kofi Annan rebuilt some faith with peace operations in Kosovo and Timor-Leste starting in 1999, and with fresh goals on poverty and AIDS. Then the American-led war in Iraq in 2003 split the security council and derailed his agenda. His successors, Ban Ki-moon and António Guterres, inherited the Syrian civil war, which divided the Council for over a decade.In 2026, the deeper problem is that the organisation increasingly appears incapable of dealing with the most consequential crises of the day and external affairs minister S Jaishankar has put the problem bluntly."Where the UN is concerned, I think it's obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked. That if you look at the big issues of the day, whether you look at the conflict in the Gulf, whether you look at the conflict in Ukraine, whether you look at other issues in Africa, whether you look at Covid, actually, the United Nations has been largely irrelevant to the decision making," EAM S Jaishankar said, however noting that the UN should not disappear."We don't need no UN. The idea is not to throw away the UN, but to fix the UN," Jaishankar said.India's stand, along with other nations actively seeking an overhaul of the United Nations, gets legitimacy from the fact that the organisation has invariably remained obdurate in tackling the menace of terrorism.Pakistan, which has been a breeding ground for terrorists was recently praised by UN chief Antonio Guterres for "being a source of solidarity"."For over two decades in different roles, I have seen Pakistan as a source of solidarity and solutions. Pakistan has shown that, even in difficult circumstances, compassion and responsibility must go hand-in-hand," Guterres said, ironally adding: "We stand with Pakistan in confronting this threat of terrorism".A veto frozen in 1945The UN's original architecture reflected the balance of power at the end of World War II. Five countries, the United States, Russia, China, Britain and France, were given permanent seats on the security council and the power to veto substantive decisions.That arrangement was, by and large, understandable in 1945. However, it is increasingly difficult to defend as a permanent settlement for the world of 2026.UN membership has expanded from 51 founding members to 193, with most of the growth coming from newly independent and smaller states. Yet the central political structure of the organisation has barely adapted to this transformation.The result is an uncomfortable contradiction as almost every country has an equal vote in the general assembly, but five countries retain an extraordinary ability to prevent collective action in the security council. The veto has repeatedly become an instrument of national interest rather than a mechanism for preserving international peace. When one of the permanent members is directly involved in a conflict, or regards an issue as strategically important, the council is rendered paralysed.The consequences are particularly serious because the nature of global insecurity has also changed. Conflict is no longer confined to battlefields. Choking Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb has disrupted energy supplies, food prices, shipping routes, financial markets and global trade. Russia and Ukraine war impacted hugely the grains supply.After the quarter of the 21st century, cyberattacks on infrastructure and banking systems, technological competition, nuclear modernisation, climate shocks and transnational crime increasingly cross borders. The UN therefore faces a world in which the consequences of conflict travel faster and further, while the institution responsible for managing those consequences seems crumbling under the beuraucratic bagage.Smaller states with bigger problemsThe most watched 81st assembly speech on YouTube is of Balendra Shah, Nepal's Prime Minister, who attended the meeting to narrate the world about the horrific flash flood that claimed lives of over 1,000 people in the Himalyan nation.The world watched him the most, at least three times more than Donald Trump, who belives climate change is "the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world". Consquently, America, under Donald Trump, has cut $4 billion in outstanding US pledges to the UN’s Green Climate Fund, immediately vacating its board seat.A presidential memorandum completely defunded and ordered withdrawal from 66 international organisations, including 31 UN entities like the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), and the Paris Climate Agreement.The US, responsible for roughly 20% to 25% of all global cumulative CO₂ emissions, also exited the UN's "loss and damage" climate disaster board. While Nepal suffers and US runs amok, UN remains helpless.These incidents, therefore, brings back to how UN's erosion of international restraints has been particularly dangerous for smaller states. The post-1945 system gave them something that military or economic power could not provide, a rules-based framework in which sovereignty and territorial integrity carried weight.As former Estonian President Lennart Meri quipped in the late 1990s: “The nuclear weapon of small states is international law.”That protection, however, has now dangerously weaken, with great-power rivalry has increasingly encouraged unilateral action, economic pressure and competing diplomatic blocs. Alternative groupings such as the G7 and Brics providing useful platforms, but their rise also risks shifting decision-making away from the universal system in which smaller states have a seat.ALSO READ | Trump's 48 F-35 jets for Saudi Arabia: Why is Israel uneasy and China a key concern"Institutions that cannot explain where they add value become vulnerable to indifference, and indifference in the current climate is not a passive condition — it is actively eroding the UN’s finances and political will. The UN has a liquidity crisis, which, at its core, is a crisis of confidence in the institution by its member states," said Rafael Grossi, IAEA chief, who is in the race to be the next UN chief.What the next UN chief must fixAntónio Guterres is due to leave office at the end of 2026, leaving his successor to restore confidence in a financially constrained and politically divided UN.The leadership change at the UN later this year could also offer an opportunity to reset the institution. The contenders for the UN chief post include senior UN trade official Rebeca Grynspan, International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi and Guyana's Ambassador to the UN Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett. Whoever gets the post, the focus must be on the conflict prevention, quiet diplomacy and making the organisation more accountable and efficient.The UN also needs to address overlapping agencies and focus resources on peace, humanitarian work and achievable development goals. But no reform can avoid the Security Council's outdated structure.India and Brazil have gained far greater global importance since 1945, yet remain outside permanent membership. Reforming representation and the veto will be difficult, but necessary if the UN is to remain relevant in a changed world.ALSO READ | Bombs without brakes? articles.title: Meet John Reznikoff, the US collector who owns $1 million worth of hair from Abraham Lincoln, Marilyn Monroe and Einstein
articles.summary: John Reznikoff has built one of the world's strangest historical collections: hair from some of the most famous people in history.
articles.body: John Reznikoff has built one of the world's strangest historical collections: hair from some of the most famous people in history. The Connecticut-based collector and authenticator holds the Guinness World Records title for the largest collection of hair from historical figures. When he received the record in 2001, his collection contained hair representing 115 historical figures, including Abraham Lincoln, Marilyn Monroe, Albert Einstein, John F Kennedy, Napoleon, Elvis Presley, King Charles I and Charles Dickens. Guinness valued the collection at $1 million at the time. Reznikoff, who runs the historical memorabilia business University Archives, has spent decades collecting, authenticating and documenting rare objects connected to prominent figures.How John Reznikoff started collecting famous hairReznikoff's interest in historical memorabilia began when he was young and eventually developed into a career dealing in historical documents, autographs and other collectibles. He established University Archives in 1979 and became known for examining and authenticating historical material. His interest in hair collecting grew after he acquired a large collection belonging to Margaretta Pierrepont, the wife of former US attorney general Edwards Pierrepont. The collection contained locks of hair connected to historical figures and helped spark Reznikoff's interest in preserving similar relics. Hair had long been kept as a personal memento, particularly during the 18th and 19th centuries, when a lock could serve as a tangible reminder of a loved one or famous person.Abraham Lincoln's hair came from the night of his assassinationOne of the most notable pieces associated with Reznikoff is hair from Abraham Lincoln. According to University Archives, three strands in the collection are connected to Lincoln's assassination at Ford's Theatre on April 14, 1865. The provenance traces the hair to Dr Charles Sabin Taft, one of the doctors who attended Lincoln after he was shot, and the material is accompanied by historical documentation including correspondence, auction records and contemporary reports. University Archives sold the three strands for $7,500 in February 2026, making the small relic a documented connection to one of the most consequential nights in US history.Marilyn Monroe's hair helped investigate her parentageReznikoff's collection also contains hair associated with Marilyn Monroe, whose samples later became part of an investigation into her biological father. According to University Archives, the hair came from Monroe's embalmer and DNA extracted from the sample was compared with genetic material from Francine Gifford Deir, a granddaughter of Charles Stanley Gifford, who had long been identified as a possible biological father of Monroe. The comparison was reported to support the conclusion that Gifford was Monroe's biological father, giving the preserved hair significance beyond celebrity memorabilia.Albert Einstein is among the famous names representedAlbert Einstein is another major historical figure represented in Reznikoff's collection. Guinness lists Einstein alongside Lincoln, Monroe, John F Kennedy, Napoleon, Elvis Presley, King Charles I and Charles Dickens among the figures whose hair is held in the collection. The archive therefore spans scientists, presidents, entertainers, royalty, writers and other influential figures from different periods of history.Elvis Presley hair sold for $115,120Reznikoff has also been involved in one of the most expensive hair sales ever recorded. In November 2002, a large quantity of Elvis Presley's hair sold for $115,120, including the buyer's premium. The hair had been collected by Elvis's personal barber, Homer "Gill" Gilleland, and the auction lot included letters of authenticity from several people, including Reznikoff's University Archives. Guinness World Records recognises the sale as the most expensive hair sold at an online auction.The Neil Armstrong dispute changed his collecting policyOne episode involving astronaut Neil Armstrong changed the way Reznikoff approached his unusual collection. In 2004, a representative working for Reznikoff approached Armstrong's barber, Marx Sizemore, who had been saving Armstrong's hair clippings, and Sizemore eventually sold the hair for $3,000. Armstrong later discovered the transaction and threatened legal action, with his lawyers seeking the return of the hair and other remedies. Armstrong also requested that proceeds from the transaction be donated to charity. Following the dispute, Reznikoff said he would no longer collect hair from living celebrities, and Guinness says his collecting now focuses on people who have died.His collection includes controversial historical figuresReznikoff's collection extends beyond entertainers and admired public figures. Guinness reports that it includes hair associated with Eva Braun, Adolf Hitler's wife, while he has also dealt with material connected to John Wilkes Booth, the actor who assassinated Lincoln. Reznikoff has said his approach eventually shifted from collecting only people who had positively influenced history to documenting historically significant figures regardless of how they are remembered.A collection worth millionsWhen Guinness awarded Reznikoff the record in 2001, the collection representing 115 historical figures was valued at $1 million. Guinness's 2026 profile estimates that figure would be about $1.8 million today and says the collection has probably grown considerably since then.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
