articles.title: Patrón co-founder John Paul DeJoria turned a 96-acre Texas ranch into a home for more than 120 exotic animals; when it sold for $6.93 million, the buyer inherited the herd and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter
articles.summary: A 96-acre Texas ranch once owned by Patrón Tequila co-founder John Paul DeJoria came with an unusual combination of luxury, wildlife and an underground
articles.body: A 96-acre Texas ranch once owned by Patrón Tequila co-founder John Paul DeJoria came with an unusual combination of luxury, wildlife and an underground shelter. More than 120 exotic African animals lived on the property, while the estate also had a 7,540-square-foot main house, two barns, a stocked pond, a pecan orchard and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The ranch, known as “Patrón de Paz,” was located in Dripping Springs, about 40 minutes west of Austin, and stretched along 2,600 feet of Fitzhugh Creek. According to the Houston Chronicle, the property was listed for $7.495 million in 2016 after initially being put on the market for $7.99 million. It eventually sold for $6.93 million. As reported by ABC13 Houston, television director Jonathan Nowzaradan is the buyer of the ranch.A ranch that came with more than a houseThe property was not simply a large Texas home. Its listing described it as an exotic-animal ranch, and the buyer was set to inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. According to the Houston Chronicle, the animals were part of the property when it was listed. The ranch included two barns, each with attached guest quarters, along with a stocked pond and a pecan orchard. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the animals included more than 120 exotic species and that the property was being sold with the animals and its furnishings. The estate itself covered 96 acres and overlooked Fitzhugh Creek, which feeds from Barton Creek. The main residence measured 7,540 square feet and had four bedrooms and six bathrooms. It featured wood-beamed ceilings, hardwood floors, partial stone walls and a large gourmet kitchen with a commercial-grade stove. Outside, there was a pool and spa, an outdoor kitchen and a wide porch overlooking the surrounding Hill Country.The underground shelterOne of the property's more unusual features was underground. As reported by The San Antonio Express-News, the ranch included a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter. The Austin Business Journal also described the property as having a “2,700-square underground shelter.” So, when the ranch changed hands, the buyer was getting far more than a luxury residence. The property came with its land, buildings, underground shelter and a large collection of exotic animals.The animals were part of the dealThe exotic animals were among the details that made the ranch unusual in the first place. As reported by The Houston Chronicle, the new owner would inherit more than 120 exotic African animals. The ranch was a 96-acre property with a spa pool, limestone walls and the animals. The animals included species such as gazelles, wildebeest and antelopes.Why DeJoria sold the ranchDeJoria, best known for co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems and Patrón Spirits Company, had owned Patrón de Paz since 2008, as reported by the San Antonio Express-News. Realtor Dave Murray said DeJoria's primary residence was near Lake Austin and that he had decided to sell the Dripping Springs ranch. Murray also said DeJoria owned several other homes around the world and was selling four estates at the time. DeJoria co-founded John Paul Mitchell Systems with hairdresser Paul Mitchell in 1980 and later co-founded Patrón Spirits Company in 1989. The ranch's sale meant that its next owner did not simply acquire a large piece of Texas Hill Country property. The $6.93 million deal also brought with it a ready-made exotic-animal ranch, two barns, a creekside estate, a stocked pond and a 2,700-square-foot underground shelter.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Egyptian authorities have charged six journalists working for independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh with alleged links to the outlawed Muslim
articles.body: Egyptian authorities have charged six journalists working for independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh with alleged links to the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood, days after security forces arrested the outlet’s entire newsroom, according to the BBC.The journalists were accused of joining a terrorist group, funding terrorism, publishing “fake news” and using social media to call for acts of terrorism, their lawyer Nabeh al-Ganadi said. Matsda2sh has denied the allegations.The six journalists - Abdullah Qadry, Mohammed Ashraf Abu Emeira, Islam Barakat, Omar Helal, Mohammed Mahmoud and Mohammed Adel - were arrested during raids on their homes across Egypt on September 28 and 29, according to the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR).The EIPR said five of the journalists were remanded in custody for 15 days by the State Security Prosecution, while the sixth was still being interrogated.The arrests have drawn condemnation from international human rights and press freedom groups. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) described the detention of the entire Matsda2sh newsroom as a “grave escalation” in Egypt’s campaign against independent journalism.Matsda2sh, whose name means “Do Not Believe” in Arabic, was founded in 2018 and regularly fact-checks statements by Egyptian officials and carries out investigative reporting.Egypt’s interior ministry has accused the platform of seeking to destabilise the country through disinformation. It said Matsda2sh was unlicensed, operated from abroad and that its founder, Abdel Rahman Mansour, was a member of the Muslim Brotherhood.Mansour has denied any connection with the group, saying the allegations “misrepresent who we are and the work we do”.The case took a more serious turn after the EIPR said the detained journalists had told prosecutors they were tortured at National Security Agency facilities following their arrests. The allegations included beatings, forced stripping, electric shocks and threats against them or their families.The interior ministry denied the allegations, with a ministry source calling them “unfounded” and saying they were aimed at evading the charges.Egypt has faced years of criticism over its treatment of journalists and political opponents. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi has overseen a broad crackdown on dissent since the military ousted former president Mohamed Morsi, a senior Muslim Brotherhood figure, in 2013.The Muslim Brotherhood was designated a terrorist organisation by Egypt following Morsi’s ouster. Tens of thousands of people have since been detained, including Brotherhood members and supporters as well as activists, academics and media workers.The arrests come amid continued concerns over press freedom in Egypt. According to the CPJ, the country currently has 25 journalists imprisoned or detained.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Nana Patekar’s legacy beyond films: How his water project made a drought-hit Marathwada village tanker-free
articles.summary: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: As film lovers across India mourned the death of veteran actor Nana Patekar on Thursday, a village in central Maharashtra
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: As film lovers across India mourned the death of veteran actor Nana Patekar on Thursday, a village in central Maharashtra remembered how his support helped it become "tanker-free" by funding a water conservation project a decade ago.Patekar, 76, passed away at his Goa residence in the early hours of Thursday, news agency PTI reported.NAAM Foundation, set up by Patekar and fellow Marathi actor Makarand Anaspure, adopted Dhondalgaon village in Vaijapur tehsil in 2016.The village, located 57km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city, would require water supplied through tankers every year as the monsoon ended and Diwali approached, river expert Anand Asolkar said.During the Nizam era, Dhondalgaon was known for its sweet limes, which were transported to other parts of the country from the nearby Karanjgaon railway station.However, silt-filled barrages on the local river made it difficult to cultivate sweet lime trees or grow more than one crop a year, PTI reported."After establishing the NAAM Foundation, Makarand Anaspure and Nana Patekar were in search of a village where a water conservation project could be undertaken. I told them about Dhondalgaon. They came here on October 2, 2015, and inaugurated the work," Asolkar told PTI."There were 12 barrages and they were completely filled with silt, so no water stopped there. The villagers also contributed to the work and we desilted a stretch of 4.5 km. It created storage capacity of nearly 20 crore litres of water," he said.The project changed the village's economy, Asolkar said."Almost 70% of farmers here now grow two crops in a year; some even grow three crops. The village has been tanker-free from 2016 to this day, except for a few months in 2018 when there was a severe drought," he said.Rahul Sable, a local activist, said the availability of water also boosted dairy farming, PTI reported.The village now produces up to 10,000 litres of milk every day, among the highest in the district, while the milk business provides employment to nearly 800 local youths."Nana adopted our village, and the way people looked at our village changed. Politicians began to give priority to the development of our village. I take pride in saying that not a single farmer suicide has taken place here since this work was completed," Sable said.Bharat Aware, the village sarpanch, said repeated droughts had led to a negative mindset among local people.However, the water conservation project led by NAAM Foundation changed everything.(With agency inputs)Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: ECoR turns scrap into artwork to beautify stations, rly premises
articles.summary: East Coast Railway turns metal scrap into public art, installing sculptures at stations like Puri, Bhubaneswar and Sambalpur to promote reuse and beautify premises.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: The East Coast Railway (ECoR) has begun converting metal scrap from its workshops and yards into artwork, with sculptures being made for display at major stations, offices and other railway premises across the zone.Officials said the initiative aims to promote the reuse of discarded materials while improving the appearance of railway spaces used by passengers and staff. Old metal parts, worn-out components and other unusable workshop materials are being collected, sorted and shaped into decorative installations by skilled workers and artists associated with railway units.“Many small pieces of scrap remain idle after e-auction. These pieces are being used to create beautiful artworks. Major stations such as Puri, Bhubaneswar and Khurda Road, along with other railway premises, will get scrap-based sculpture installations,” an ECoR spokesperson said.One such sculpture has already been completed at Sambalpur station and opened for public viewing.Several other pieces are being prepared at the carriage repair workshop at Mancheswar in Bhubaneswar. Completed installations at the workshop include a large guitar and a small replica of an Air Force chopper, both fabricated from discarded metal parts. These sculptures have been installed within the workshop area and have drawn attention for their creative use of materials that would otherwise have been disposed of as waste.The routine overhauling yard at Sarla station has also installed a sculpture made from scrap. A miniature model of an old railway engine has been created from scrap and installed at Kantabanji station.ECoR is also preparing a scrap-metal sculpture for display at its headquarters in Bhubaneswar. Officials said the artwork will reflect the railway’s commitment to sustainability, innovation and the beautification of public infrastructure.The project is part of a broader effort to encourage environmentally responsible practices within railway establishments. By converting scrap into creative exhibits, the zone hopes to reduce waste, support recycling and showcase the craftsmanship of railway personnel.More stations and offices may be covered under the initiative in the coming months, depending on the availability of scrap and suitable display locations. articles.title: SSA programmer nabbed by vigilance taking Rs 30,000 bribe
articles.summary: Odisha Vigilance arrested SSA programmer Chandrajit Parija in Jagatsinghpur for allegedly taking a Rs 30,000 bribe to clear digital blackboard bills.
articles.body: Kendrapada: Vigilance officials on Thursday nabbed Chandrajit Parija, programmer in the office of district education officer-cum-district project coordinator (DEO-cum-DPC), Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Jagatsinghpur, while allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs 30,000 from an executant for facilitating the release of pending bills.Vigilance sources said Parija demanded the bribe for clearing bills related to the installation of digital blackboards in schools across Jagatsinghpur district. As a member of the procurement and technical committee, he was responsible for inspecting the installation work and certifying it, following which the bills were to be released in favour of the executant.The complainant allegedly approached Parija several times seeking inspection of the completed work. However, instead of taking steps to inspect the work, Parija allegedly demanded Rs 30,000 for processing and clearing the pending bills. Following the alleged demand, the complainant reported the matter to the vigilance authorities.Acting on the complaint, Odisha Vigilance laid a trap and caught Parija while he was allegedly accepting the bribe from the complainant on Thursday. The entire tainted amount was seized from him. articles.title: In 1928, supporters had raised $5 million for Great Smoky Mountains National Park but rising land prices stalled the effort; a Rockefeller memorial fund matched it with another $5 million, helping make the park possible
articles.summary: Explore the inspiring story of how $5 million raised for the creation of Great Smoky Mountains National Park stalled due to rising land prices until the Rockefeller family matched it with another $5 million, making the park a reality.
articles.body: Great Smoky Mountains National Park stretches across more than 522,000 acres along the Tennessee-North Carolina border. But its creation faced a major hurdle when rising land prices pushed the cost of acquiring the forest beyond what supporters had raised.By 1928, supporters had raised $5 million to purchase land for the proposed park. But land prices had risen sharply, doubling the cost of the property and bringing the campaign to a standstill.The breakthrough came when the Laura Spelman Rockefeller Memorial Fund donated another $5 million. The gift matched the money already raised and helped supporters buy the remaining land needed to establish the park.A park that had to be boughtThe idea of creating a national park in the Great Smoky Mountains had been around since the late 1890s. Supporters wanted to protect the forests and mountains of the Southern Appalachians for future generations.But unlike some of the older national parks in the western US, the government did not already own the land.The Smokies were home to hundreds of farmers, while large timber and paper companies controlled huge areas of forest. Buying the land meant convincing families to sell their farms and companies to give up forests, rail tracks, logging equipment, and other property.There was also a debate over whether the area should become a national forest or a national park. A national forest could allow activities such as timber cutting and grazing, while a national park would give greater priority to protecting the landscape and natural resources.Motorists helped drive the campaignThe campaign gained momentum in the 1920s, with major support coming from Knoxville, Tennessee, and Asheville, North Carolina.The two cities had competed over where the park should be located, but eventually backed a plan to protect a large area between them.Car owners also became important supporters. Automobile clubs wanted better roads through scenic parts of the country, and the growing popularity of cars made the mountains easier for visitors to reach.In May 1926, President Calvin Coolidge signed legislation providing for the creation of Great Smoky Mountains National Park and Shenandoah National Park, as per the National Park Service (NPS).The law said the Interior Department could take responsibility for the Smokies once 150,000 acres had been purchased.Because the government could not simply buy the land for the proposed park, supporters had to raise the money themselves.$5 million was not enoughTennessee and North Carolina each contributed $2 million towards buying the land. Individuals, private groups and even schoolchildren also contributed.By 1928, the campaign had collected $5 million.But the money was no longer enough. Land prices had doubled, leaving supporters without enough funds to complete the purchases.That was when the Rockefeller family stepped in.John D. Rockefeller Jr., who had supported the creation of parks in the eastern United States, suggested that the Laura Spelman Rockefeller Memorial Fund donate $5 million in memory of his mother.The donation matched the $5 million already raised and helped the campaign purchase the remaining land.About 85% of the park's land was eventually bought from 18 logging companies. The rest came from about 1,200 individual landowners. Some people were allowed to continue living on their former properties under lifetime leases.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Govt plans to push homestays in Ganjam coastal villages
articles.summary: Odisha government plans homestays in five Ganjam coastal villages near Blue Flag Sonapur beach, offering Tourism Policy-2026 subsidies and investor incentives.
articles.body: Berhampur: To boost local tourism and provide visitors with an authentic and cultural experience, the state govt has planned to develop homestay facilities in five fishermen-dominated villages in Ganjam district’s Chikit block.The selected villages include Sonapur, Katura, Surala, Jhatipadara and Eksingh — all seashore villages. Govt will provide incentive and subsidy schemes under its new Tourism Policy-2026 to attract investors to provide homestay facilities.Located at the confluence of Bahuda river and Bay of Bengal, about 30 km from Berhampur, Sonapur beach has been certified as a Blue Flag beach for the past three years in a row as it meets stringent international standards for cleanliness, environmental sustainability, safety, etc., due to the active participation of the local people and has become a model for sustainable coastal tourism.To provide homestay facilities to visitors who visit Sonapur, govt has selected its adjoining villages and has proposed 15 homestays in these villages, sources said.“The investors’ meet will be held at Chhatrapur in the district on Friday to discuss the state’s new tourism policy and different schemes under the policy, including homestay facilities,” said Ganjam collector Keerthi Vasan V.Around 250 investors are expected to participate in the meet, where the state’s tourism commissioner-cum-secretary Balwant Singh is scheduled to attend. Under the new tourism policy, each homestay project will receive financial assistance. The investor will get a Rs 2.5 lakh subsidy per room, etc., sources said. The homestay owners will also be extended support for capacity building, marketing facilities, etc.Apart from homestays, other investment opportunities in tourism sectors in the district are likely to be discussed in the meeting, sources said.Known for its scenic beauty and tourist attractions, Ganjam district offers a memorable experience for visitors. “Famous tourist destinations, including Gopalpur and Sonapur beach, famous Shakti shrine Tara Tarini, Taptapani, famous for its hot spring, Jaugada and Potagada — historical monuments, Biranachi Narayan temple, known as wooden Konark, etc., have attracted tourists from the country and abroad throughout the year,” said Janak Kumar Tarai, district tourist officer.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news.
